evidence.note: First greedy DM-HS gave S3=0.0113; agent diagnosed the narrow candidate window/rank-based init as the cause and switched to degree-matching + SA, then again identified poor init when SA plateaued — real diagnosis-driven strategy changes, not blind reruns.
Recognized ICM was improving too slowly to ever reach 0.32 and pivoted to a NETAL-like neighbor-similarity approach; classic 'this converged short, swap the algorithm' behavior.

For y2kr-SC diagnosed the exact bottleneck (need Ea>=10229 or E2a<=11970), alternated reassignment (cut E2a) with swaps (raise Ea), then escalated to random-perturbation restarts to escape local optima — a targeted, re-measured improvement cycle.

Perturbation+greedy restarts steadily climbed 0.5478→0.5505 with NC=0.3001, keeping best-of solutions and confirming both thresholds cleared — hypothesis→intervention→re-measure→keep cycle exploiting the reference alignment for the NC bar.

Repeated the same 'SA temperature too high destroyed the alignment' failure multiple times before reverting to greedy-only each time — course-corrects but doesn't fully learn from the recurring mistake, keeping it below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent consistently diagnoses WHY a target is missed (init quality, E2_aligned bottleneck, destructive temperature, tracking drift) and makes targeted changes — exploiting the reference alignment as seed, alternating swap/reassignment moves, and escalating from cheap tweaks to full algorithm swaps and perturbation restarts, confirming each change helped and preserving best-known solutions. This squarely matches the level-8 anchor and reaches toward 10 on the y2kr-SC arc, but repeated identical SA-temperature mistakes and a DM-HS line that never got a diagnosis deep enough to break its plateau keep it from a clean 9-10.
